attributes.negative_finding: MBRenderText's ent->rec (MBBlitEnt.rec, a u8[0x18] glyph sub-record with documented px/py/depth/u/v sub-offsets) resisted every de-fakematch form tried, bisected to 4 distinct probes: (1) typed `MBBlitRec rec;` struct member replacing all 7 sites: real 74->96. (2) offsetof()-renaming all 7 sites on the unchanged raw u8[] (no typed intermediate): real 74->96, same magnitude as (1). (3) offsetof() on depth+u+v only (3 sites), px/py left bare-hex: real 74->84. (4) offsetof() on depth alone (1 site, replacing bare '8'): real 74->76. All four regressed; reverted to the original all-bare-hex form (real restored to 74, confirmed via defake_gate). This contradicts claim.law.offsetof-rename-preserves-protected-web's 'near-guaranteed neutral' verdict for probe (4) in particular (a single-occurrence rename, the law's easiest case) -- filed as a new boundary-case law (see laws_applied) since the base pointer here (`ent->rec`, an array-typed struct member accessed through `->`) differs from every prior verified-neutral offsetof-rename precedent (all on a simple pointer variable). A second, independent single-occurrence offsetof rename in the SAME pass (MBFontStringWidth's specialFont+offsetof(MBFontState,fonts), also on a plain pointer VARIABLE) stayed byte-identical, sharpening the boundary to array-member vs pointer-variable bases specifically rather than 'single occurrence' being the safe/unsafe axis.
